note: Lines for visitors (G7 road folk, H9 notoriety callers) and legitimacy voices (E3). Placeholders: {speaker} {name} {first} {town} {home} {to} {creed} {item} {qty} {coin} {patron} {leader} {doctrine} {promise}. News lines open with {speaker} so a named townsperson carries them at dawn.

reason.pilgrim: bound for the chapel at {to}, keeping {creed}
reason.tax_collector: come for the tax on what you carry
reason.beggar: come in from {home} with an empty bowl
reason.petitioner: come from {home} to ask your help

pilgrim: To the chapel at {to}. I keep {creed}, and it keeps me.
{to}, for the chapel. Three days of walking for one evening of quiet.
courier: Word from {home} for {to}. I don't read it, I only carry it.
{to}, and quick about it. {home} has things to say.
refugee: Away from {home}. {to}, if they'll have us.
Anywhere but {home}. They say {to} still has bread.
pedlar: {to}. They're short of {item} there, and I'm long on it.
Down to {to} with {item}. A fair price and a dry bed, that's all I want.
arrived: I'm here now. A day or two, then on.
This is where the road ended. For now.

setout_pilgrim: {speaker} says a pilgrim, {name}, is on the road to {to}.
setout_courier: {speaker} says a courier set out from {home} with word for {to}.
setout_refugee: {speaker} says folk are on the road out of {home}. {first} among them.
setout_pedlar: {speaker} says a pedlar left {home} with {item} for {to}.
arrive_pilgrim: {speaker} says a pilgrim came in at dawn, {name}, here for the chapel.
arrive_courier: {speaker} says a courier came in off the road with word from {home}.
arrive_refugee: {speaker} says {name} walked in from {home} with nothing but a bundle.
arrive_pedlar: {speaker} says a pedlar, {name}, came in and sold {item} at the store.
settled_refugee: {speaker} says {name} means to stay. Someone found them a corner.
tax_collector: {speaker} says a tax collector, {name}, is in town asking after you.
patron_man: {speaker} says the {patron}'s man, {name}, is waiting on you by the square.
thief: {speaker} says there's a stranger, {first}, who keeps looking at the cellars.
spy: {speaker} says someone called {first} has been asking about your dealings.
beggar: {speaker} says {name} came in from {home} with an empty bowl.
petitioner: {speaker} says {name} walked over from {home} to ask you something.
beggar_local: {speaker} says {name} is sitting by the hearth with an empty bowl.
petitioner_local: {speaker} says {name} has been waiting all morning to ask you something.

ask_tax_collector: {coin} coin, on what you carry and what you keep. I don't make the rule.
The count says {coin}. Pay me and I'm gone by morning.
pay_tax: That's the tax. I'll trouble you no more this season.
Counted and right. Good day to you.
refuse_tax: Refuse, then. Your name goes in the book, and the book gets read.
Suit yourself. Word travels faster than I do.
ask_patron_man: The {patron} says you owe them. {coin} coin squares it, for now.
The {patron} keeps good books. {coin} coin, and they'll stop asking.
pay_patron: The {patron} will be glad. Glad is better than the other thing.
Paid. I'll tell them you were easy.
refuse_patron: I'll tell the {patron} what you said. Word for word.
That's a long memory you've just made.
ask_thief: Just passing. Admiring the doors round here.
Me? I'm nobody. Nobody at all.
confront_thief: All right, all right. I'm going. You've a loud voice.
Easy. I never touched a thing. I'll be off.
pay_thief: Generous. I'll find another town to admire.
That'll do. You never saw me.
ask_spy: Who's asking? Only curious. Who do you deal with, then?
Just a traveller. Who did you say your patrons were?
tale_spy: Is that so. Not much to write home about, then.
Hm. Nothing worth the walk. I'll tell them so.
send_spy: No need to shout. I've what I came for.
ask_beggar: Nothing since yesterday. It's bad in {home}.
A coin, a crust. Whatever you can spare.
coin_beggar: Thank you. I won't forget a face like yours.
food_beggar: Oh. Oh, that's warm. Thank you.
Food. I'd nearly forgotten the taste.
ask_petitioner: We're short of {item} in {home}. {coin} coin would see us right. Folk say you can.
In {home} we've no {item} to speak of. If you'd see to it, {coin} coin's worth, we'd remember.
help_petitioner: You will? Then {home} will hear your name said kindly.
Thank you. I'll walk back with good news for once.
refuse_petitioner: I see. I'll tell them I asked.
Then I've walked a long way for nothing.
bless_pilgrim: Go warm. The chapel asks nothing more.
A blessing, then. Keep it near the fire.
blessed_pilgrim: I've given what I had. Walk well.
One blessing a road. That's the rule.
food_refugee: You're kind. The little ones will eat.
Thank you. I'll pass the kindness on when I can.
coin_refugee: It'll get us to {to}. Thank you.
Coin for the road. I won't waste it.
point_refugee: {to}, past the stones. I'll find it. I'll stay, if they'll have me.
Thank you. Knowing the way is half the walk.
buy_pedlar: Good {item}, that. Mind how you carry it.
Sold. Pleasure doing business on the road.
sold_out_pedlar: Empty now. You had the last of it.
Nothing left to sell. Lighter walking, though.
answered: Nothing more to say. I'll be gone by morning.

townNews.war: they're at war with {other}, and it's going badly
townNews.despair: it's grey there, and getting greyer
townNews.calm: the {doctrine} is {standing}, and the bread comes

dawn_firm: {speaker} says {leader} has the whole town behind them now. "{promise}", and it's true.
{speaker} says nobody would hear a word against {leader} today.
dawn_kept: {speaker} says {leader} does right by folk, mostly. The {doctrine} holds.
{speaker} says the {doctrine} keeps its word more often than not.
dawn_habit: {speaker} says people follow {leader} out of habit now, not faith.
{speaker} says "{promise}" sounds thinner every time {leader} says it.
dawn_doubt: {speaker} says folk mutter about {leader} at the well. "{promise}", they laugh.
{speaker} says few still believe in the {doctrine}. It could fall any day.
dawn_fallen: {speaker} says nobody keeps the {doctrine} now. {leader} keeps to the house.
ask_firm: {leader}? I'd stand up for them in front of anyone.
We've never had it better. "{promise}", and they meant it.
ask_kept: {leader} does right by us, mostly. Mostly's not bad.
The {doctrine} holds. Some weeks better than others.
ask_habit: We go along with {leader}. What else is there?
ask_doubt: Promises. That's all the {doctrine} is now. Promises.
ask_fallen: Nobody keeps it now. We muddle through on our own.
It fell. I can't say I miss it.
ask_none: No compact here. We keep our own counsel.
Nobody leads us. Nobody's needed to.
remark_firm: Say what you like, {leader} keeps their word.
remark_habit: Same old words from {leader}. Same old hunger.
We follow because we always have.
remark_doubt: If {leader} promised me the sunrise I'd check the sky.
remark_fallen: Nobody's in charge now. Strange, how quiet it is.
